gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AC ratings it lined up are different kinds of figure: Jackery (2,200 W, 4,400 W surge) and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max (2,400 W, 4,800 W surge) publish surge ratings, but BLUETTI's Elite 200 V2 publishes no surge figure and its higher number (3,900 W 'Power Lifting') is only for pure resistive loads. The cycle-life claims also use different endpoints (BLUETTI 6,000+ cycles to 80%; EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max 3,000+ cycles to 80%).
standout_why: StormWatts (cited in both chats) lists solar caps, voltage windows and series/parallel wiring for 24 kits, so wiring is already covered. It says it gives no cycle life and no AC continuous or surge figure for any kit. ChatGPT's two answers put BLUETTI '2,600W output' next to Jackery '2,200W' and EcoFlow '2,400W' with no surge column and no cycle-life endpoint. I could not fetch our own two Dealectric pages (the fetch tool hit a certificate error and the curl download was not approved), so I have not checked whether they already give cycle endpoints. solargenreview.com returned HTTP 429. I did not open wearesalt.org or lightsonlabs.com because of the call budget.
decides: For starting motors (fridge, sump pump), ChatGPT's ranking of the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 above Jackery 2000 v2 and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max on '2,600 W output' may not hold. Jackery and EcoFlow publish 2× surge ratings; BLUETTI's 3,900 W applies only to resistive loads like kettles and heaters, and it publishes no surge figure. On battery life, BLUETTI's 6,000+ cycles to 80% is the strongest claim stated to the stricter endpoint. Shipping matters more for the pick: the Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W kit is a pre-order (ships from Nov 26, link price $1,424.05). The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Solar Generator showed as available at $1,229 on EcoFlow's store, but I did not confirm which panels that price includes.
